name: Baroque
summary: Classical orders bent into curves: oval plans, convex and concave fronts, doubled columns and light that drops from hidden windows. Bernini, Borromini and the court architects built it as theatre to move the viewer.

philosophy.core_thesis: Architecture should move the viewer: curve, depth, light and ornament make one dramatic effect, in the service of church and crown.
design_principles: Replace the circle and the square by the oval, and the straight front by a convex or concave wall of 1 to 3m curve depth.
Use the giant order, a column or pilaster of 2 to 3 storeys, and double or group the columns in pairs.
Break the entablature and the pediment forward and back at each bay, so that the cornice casts a deep shadow.
Light the focal point from a hidden source: a lantern, a concealed window or a gilded burst above the altar.
Lead the eye on a strong axis, with a series of rooms or a stair that grows in richness toward a climax.
Unite architecture, sculpture and painting: a ceiling fresco, stucco figures and gilding in one surface.
anti_patterns: Flat, calm fronts that keep every part in one plane
Plain unornamented walls with no sculpture or fresco
Pointed Gothic arches or thin skeletal structure
Strict small-module grids with no curve
Even, shadowless light from large plain windows
A single order stacked in equal bays with no central emphasis

massing.form: A sculpted block with a curved front, a central dome or lantern, and projecting wings; plans use ovals and interlocking curves.
massing.proportion: A front of 1:1 to 3:2, with a central bay 1.5 to 2 times wider than its neighbours and rising above them.
massing.roof: A tall dome on a drum with a lantern, or a mansard roof with sculpted dormers and statues on the balustrade.
massing.relation_to_ground: A sweeping flight of steps, a piazza or a cour d'honneur that draws the visitor on to the central door.

structure.system: Load-bearing masonry with brick and stone vaults and domes, hidden behind plaster and stucco.
structure.span_and_module: Bays of 4 to 6m, with piers of 1 to 1.5m; oval naves of 15 to 25m on the long axis.
structure.expression: The structure is hidden. Orders and curves express movement and not load.

materials.finish: Rich and sculpted: polished marble, gilding, painted ceilings and moulded stucco on every surface.

facade.composition: A front that swells and recedes in a convex or concave curve, with paired columns, a broken pediment and a central niche or window.
facade.openings: Windows framed by pediments of alternating triangle and arc, with deep reveals; the window-to-wall ratio is 15 to 30%.
facade.solid_to_void: Solid leads: 70–85% opaque, modelled by deep shadow.

light_and_space.daylight: Light from hidden windows and the lantern falls on the altar or the stair, and the rest of the room stays in shadow.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: A sequence of growing richness: portal, oval nave, then the high altar or the state stair at the climax of the axis.
light_and_space.interior_character: Fresco vaults that open to a painted sky, gilded stucco, curved galleries and polished coloured marble.

ornament.attitude: Ornament is abundant and dramatic: sculpture, gilding and painting fuse with the structure to make one rich effect.

rules.rule: Draw all lines to one climax, the altar or the central stair, and light it from a hidden source.
Hide the light source in a lantern or a concealed window, and keep the walls dim.
Build the front in 3 to 5 planes that project and recede.
Pair the columns and swell the bays to a strong beat.
Hold bilateral symmetry on the axis, and bend the walls inside it.
Use the giant order over 2 to 3 storeys to overwhelm the viewer.

emotion.target_response: Wonder and awe: the viewer feels carried up and in by a staged, overflowing display of power and faith.

avoid_when: The brief asks for restraint, a low budget or a quiet, modest building.
The design needs a flat, repeatable and modular facade.

modifiers.how: Straighten the front into one plane, replace the paired columns by a single portico, and cut the gilding and sculpture.

positive: ceiling fresco open to the sky
dramatic light from a hidden lantern

canonical_works.work: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane, Rome
Palace of Versailles, Hall of Mirrors

roof_pitch.note: The range covers a dome on a drum and a mansard roof.

sources.title: Rudolf Wittkower, Art and Architecture in Italy 1600–1750 (Yale University Press, 1958)
